result.title: Learning When to Trust and Reobserve Sparse-Frame VideoQA from Temporal Sampling Perturbations
result.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Physical Understanding for Decision-Making (PhysUnderstand), Poster
result.summary: Sparse-frame video-language models can change their answers when only the sampling timestamps shift. Raw agreement exposes this problem, but it need not rank errors better than token confidence or identify which additional observation will repair an answer. We argue that answer risk and action value must be estimated separately. PhaseGuard+ probes a frozen VLM at controlled temporal offsets, predicts the reliability of the phase-vote answer, and predicts the example-wise correctness gain of a specific rescue action. The second score routes only examples expected to benefit from denser frames or a stronger VLM. Both predictors use lightweight models trained on public data; the VLMs remain frozen. We use 256 Perception Test videos for method development and evaluate on a disjoint 256-video test set comprising 554 Physics questions. For Qwen3-VL-8B, reliability AUROC rises from 68.0% with token softmax to 74.8% (+6.8 pp, 95% CI [2.6, 10.7] pp). Routing 30% of questions to Qwen3-VL-32B reaches 67.87% accuracy, compared with 63.66% for budget-matched random routing (+4.21 percentage points, CI [1.89, 6.40]). All four tested rescue pairs significantly outperform random routing. Temporal sensitivity becomes actionable when the system learns both whether an answer is unreliable and whether an available action is likely to fix it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究稀疏帧 VideoQA 中仅采样时间戳变化就导致答案翻转的问题，提出 PhaseGuard+：在受控时间偏移上探测冻结 VLM，用轻量模型分别预测相位投票答案的可靠性，以及某个「补救动作」（加密帧或换更强模型）的逐样本正确性增益，并按后者只路由预期受益的样本。
AI.relevance_reason: 把「答案是否可信」与「再观察是否有价值」拆成两个分数，直接对应 LVR 关注的 LOOK/STOP 决策与证据获取的成本收益权衡；可供核查其可靠性预测是否优于 token 置信度、以及动作价值估计能否迁移为 latent 状态下的停止与再观察准则。
